standard_prerequisites.name: Well-ordering minimal-element property
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same unit, the definition of a well-order together with the preceding proposition wo:strictorder (source lines 1250-1263)
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof opens the contrapositive by collecting the counterexamples into a non-empty set X and invoking that X has a <-minimal element; this is exactly the well-ordering property packaged by wo:strictorder (every non-empty subset has a least member).

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1265-1271): if < well-orders A, then for any formula phi(x), if (for all a in A)((for all b < a)phi(b) implies phi(a)), then (for all a in A)phi(a).
Contrapositive setup (proof lines 1273-1278): suppose not (for all a in A)phi(a), i.e. the set X = {x in A : not phi(x)} is non-empty.

Minimal counterexample (lines 1278-1283): X has a <-minimal element a by the well-ordering property; hence (for all b < a)phi(b) holds while not phi(a), which is precisely the negation of the induction conclusion - completing the contrapositive.
proof_roadmap: Assume the schema fails and form the non-empty set X of counterexamples.
Take the <-minimal element a of X via the well-ordering property.
Read off that every b < a satisfies phi while a does not, completing the contrapositive.

H2: routine minimal-element argument.
